note: Registration context across the supplier boundary, now with a skill split. ResourcefulLib's FabricRegistryEntry.of evaluates a mod's Supplier and only then registers, so the id exists on the factory's stack but not inside the lambda that builds Item.Settings (runs/p258). Two rules bridge that gap: replace the supplier call with one that carries registry+id, and route settings construction through a factory that reads the active context. The settings redirect DECLINES any method that calls Registry.register, because registrationKeys owns those - it can see the id, this rule cannot (runs/p260, runs/p263).

insertBeforeCalls.evidence: runs/p258: in FabricRegistryEntry.of, aload_1 (the Identifier) is at offset 4/6 and Supplier.get at 8, with the registry in local 0. The replacement pushes registry then id, so the new descriptor consumes supplier+registry+id in that order. The bridge restores the previous context in a finally block, so a patched class cannot set it and forget to clear it.

constructorRedirects.evidence: The factory returns a keyed Settings when a context is active and a plain one otherwise. Declines methods that call Registry.register: there registrationKeys injects the key itself (it has the id in scope), and replacing the constructor first would strip that rule of its target - the conflict measured in runs/p260 and split in runs/p263.
